_comment: Pinned schema-bridge generator binaries from ley-line-open releases.
The DIGEST is the trust root, not the tag. A tag is mutable and a release
asset can be replaced under a stable tag name; the failure would be silent
because generated output looks plausible either way. This is the same
lesson as the OCI mutable-tag work (cloister-195e47) and the stale
generator pin it replaces (cloister-9170d0), where a v0.7.9 plugin
regenerated cluster.zod.ts green for five minor versions.
SHA256SUMS ships in the release too, but it is NOT the trust root: it
comes from the same place as the binary, so a compromised release supplies
both. These digests were captured out-of-band and are what a download is
checked against.
capnpc-schema-bridge-tooldefs is pinned here even though no `task` invokes it:
it emits src/generated/llo-execution-tools.json, which is regenerated by hand per
llo-execution-contract.lock.json. The v0.15.0 re-vendor was first performed with a
binary fetched straight from the release — unverified — which is exactly the input
this file exists to refuse. A generator used only by humans still decides what gets
committed, so it needs the same pin as one used by a task.
Bumping: change version, replace ALL digests, run `task schema-bridge:fetch`
on one platform to confirm, and regenerate. A digest that does not match
fails the build closed.
`wasm` pins the platform-independent wasm32 modules the Worker imports, from the
SAME release (cloister-dbe9c3). They replace building LLO's crates for wasm32
inside cloister. Same trust rule: the digest here, not SHA256SUMS, is the root.
`task llo:wasm` verifies and places them at rs/target/llo-wasm/<name>.
`leyline-krun-worker` is not a generator: it is LLO's microVM worker, which
`cloister runtime install` places beside cloister-host-runtime (cloister-991e65).
LLO publishes it for darwin-arm64 only, so it pins only that platform; the
platforms a family needs are read from this file, never from a fixed list.
